messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: chains in parallel
parts:
Hi,

Is there a currently supported way to safely do chains in parallel
with a multicore processor? Apparently, the naive approach is a very
BAD idea

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ for CHAIN in {1..5}; do demo/wawro --
data_file=/opt/wawro/stan/wawro2.dump --sample_file="sample$CHAIN.csv"
& done

because the 5 .csv files are identical.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] chains in parallel
parts:
You've hit two things on my to-do list for the release.

I'm actually surprised running parallel processes
didn't work. There shouldn't be any interference.
I don't know much about how for-loops work in the shell.

1. Allow random seeds to be specified per chain.

2. Allow real multi-threading. It doesn't look like
you need this.

I don't know a portable way to run multi-threading easily.

I've tested thread local variables for the auto-dif
stack (the only issue for multi-threading in our code),
and it gives you about a 20% performance hit in my testing,
but will work. It's not really configurable in the current
design, but I'd like to change that.

- Bob
